_comment:
Uses this widget's own token, then the variable token_env names, which defaults to $GITHUB_TOKEN. It does not read any other widget's section: a token here and a different one under `github` is an ordinary thing to want, and borrowing would run this widget on a credential its own settings screen never showed.

Empty accounts discovers the viewer login and every org they belong to.

Empty repos means recently-pushed repos that have workflow files, capped at max_repos per owner so one busy org cannot hide personal — never every repo the token can see. The screen names the cap.
_token_comment: This widget's GitHub token. Empty falls through to the variable token_env names, not to another widget's token.
_token_env_comment: Which environment variable holds the token, when `token` is empty. Defaults to GITHUB_TOKEN. This is a variable name, never a credential.
_enterprise_hostname_comment: Web hostname of a GitHub Enterprise Cloud tenant (for example acme.ghe.com). A *.ghe.com host is called at api.<host>. Empty reads the variable enterprise_hostname_env names, if any; otherwise github.com.
_enterprise_hostname_env_comment: Name of an environment variable to read when enterprise_hostname is empty, for example GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_HOSTNAME. Empty reads none. This is a variable name, never a hostname.
_accounts_comment: GitHub users or organizations to inspect; empty discovers the viewer and their organizations.
_repos_comment: Explicit owner/repository names; empty discovers recently pushed repositories with workflows.
_window_hours_comment: Hours of workflow runs included in summaries.
_max_repos_comment: Maximum discovered repositories inspected per account.
_pushed_days_comment: How recently a repository must have been pushed to qualify for discovery.
_share_readings_comment:
Share what GitHub said with every other github-actions pane on this machine, so several panes make one request per repository per refresh between them instead of one each. On by default.

Without it every pane asks for every repository itself: with a few dozen repositories one pane spends more than half of GitHub's 5,000 requests an hour, and two panes go over.

The readings are kept in one file in ~/.local/state/opscope, readable only by you: who the token belongs to, the repositories found, and each repository's runs in the window, run titles included. A reading nobody has refreshed for 2 hours is deleted; the token itself is never stored. A spent rate limit stops every pane until GitHub's reset, and each pane says when it will ask again. Turn it off to have this pane ask on its own; the line under the status line says which it is doing.
